questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T (inside the quadrilateral), and ∠STR = 8°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 7 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the other two angles.

∴ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ 8° = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 16°

Given ratio of ∠P : ∠Q = 7 : 9. Sum of ratio parts = 7 + 9 = 16 units.

Since 16 units = 16°, then 1 unit = 1°.

Difference between ∠Q and ∠P = 9 − 7 = 2 units = 2°.

**∴ The correct answer is 2°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at T.

∠STR = 8°

Ratio of ∠P : ∠Q = 7 : 9

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/342973b192a53d07ccbdd5f1027e7efd2e2dc5b4c406fe3c7e8a993d0d8b10de.png] 

**Calculations:**

In ▵STR:

⇒ ∠STR + ∠TSR + ∠TRS = 180°

Since ST and RT are the bisectors of ∠S and ∠R respectively:

⇒ ∠TSR = ∠S ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TRS = ∠R ÷ 2

Substituting these values in the triangle angle sum equation:

⇒ 8° + (∠S ÷ 2) + (∠R ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 8°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 172°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 344°

In quadrilateral PQRS, the sum of all interior angles is 360°:

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 344° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 360° − 344°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 16°

Given that the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 7 : 9, let ∠P = 7x and ∠Q = 9x:

⇒ 7x + 9x = 16°

⇒ 16x = 16°

⇒ x = 1°

Therefore, the measures of the angles are:

⇒ ∠P = 7 × 1° = 7°

⇒ ∠Q = 9 × 1° = 9°

The difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P is:

⇒ ∠Q − ∠P = 9° − 7° = 2°

**Option Analysis:**

• **Option (1) 0.5°:** Incorrect. If the difference were 0.5°, then 2x = 0.5° ⇒ x = 0.25°, which would mean ∠P + ∠Q = 16 × 0.25° = 4°, contradicting the given ∠STR = 8°.

• **Option (2) 4°:** Incorrect. If the difference were 4°, then 2x = 4° ⇒ x = 2°, which would mean ∠P + ∠Q = 16 × 2° = 32°, contradicting the given ∠STR = 8°.

• **Option (3) 2°:** Correct. This value perfectly satisfies the angle sum property and the given angle bisector relation.

• **Option (4) 7°:** Incorrect. If the difference were 7°, then 2x = 7° ⇒ x = 3.5°, which would mean ∠P + ∠Q = 16 × 3.5° = 56°, contradicting the given ∠STR = 8°.

**∴ The correct answer is 2°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem in Quadrilaterals

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles: ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2.

Sum of Interior Angles of a Polygon

For any n-sided polygon, the sum of interior angles is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is 360°.

Opposite Angle Bisectors

The angle between the bisectors of two opposite angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the difference of the other two angles.</p

questions.question: The simplified value of 74 - 3 × (21 + 15) + 36 is:
The median of the observations 85, 62, 20, 72, 20, 43, 35, 90, 68, 56 and 79 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the **11 observations** in ascending order:

20, 20, 35, 43, 56, **62**, 68, 72, 79, 85, 90

Since the number of terms (N = 11) is odd, the median is the middle term:

Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **62**

**∴ The correct answer is 62.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 85, 62, 20, 72, 20, 43, 35, 90, 68, 56, 79

Total number of observations (N) = 11

**Formula Used:**

When N is odd, **Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation after arranging in ascending order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bde88f3aae19202cd42664ed333510508e55725b3858b610382f208da5744016.png] 

**Calculations:**

Arrange the given observations in **ascending order**:

⇒ 20, 20, 35, 43, 56, 62, 68, 72, 79, 85, 90

Count the total number of observations:

⇒ N = 11

Since N is an **odd number**, the median is calculated as:

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

Looking at the arranged sequence, the 6th term is **62**.

Let us verify why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ Option (1) 68 is the 7th term, which is not the middle term.

⇒ Option (3) 56 is the 5th term, which is not the middle term.

⇒ Option (4) 72 is the 8th term, which is not the middle term.

**∴ The correct answer is 62.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If N is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th term and the ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th term. Formula: Median = [ (N/2)th term + (N/2 + 1)th term ] ÷ 2.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

The sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ N.

Mode

The observation that appears most frequently in the data set. For the given data, 20 appears twice, so the mode is 20.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode for moderately skewed distributions is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question: If the volume of a right circular cone of height 11 cm is 297π cm³, find the diameter of its base.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of **cone** V = (1/3)πr²h

297π = (1/3) × π × r² × 11

r² = (297 × 3) ÷ 11 = 27 × 3 = 81

r = 9 cm → **Diameter** = 2 × 9 = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height** (h) of the cone = 11 cm

**Volume** (V) of the cone = 297π cm³

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Right Circular Cone** = (1/3)πr²h

**Diameter** (d) = 2 × **Radius** (r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1717f215cc9a219820e3610a3d51d38b519b3dca52310a724cb53801afbd07df.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1/3) × π × r² × 11 = 297π

⇒ (1/3) × r² × 11 = 297

⇒ r² × 11 = 297 × 3

⇒ r² = 891 ÷ 11

⇒ r² = 81

⇒ r = √81 = 9 cm

⇒ **Diameter** = 2 × r = 2 × 9 = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of Cone

The slant height (l) is the distance from the apex to any point on the base circumference: l = √(r² + h²).

Surface Area of Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl and Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(l + r).

Volume Relation with Cylinder

The volume of a **cone** is exactly one-third the volume of a **cylinder** with the same radius and height.</p

questions.question: The temperatures recorded over five consecutive days in a town were: 28°C, 30°C, 32°C, 31°C, and 29°C. What was the average temperature during these five days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a **base temperature** of 30°C.

Find the **deviations** from 30: (28−30), (30−30), (32−30), (31−30), (29−30) → −2, 0, +2, +1, −1.

Net deviation = (−2) + 0 + (+2) + (+1) + (−1) = 0.

Average = Base + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Days) = 30 + (0 ÷ 5) = 30°C.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Recorded temperatures for **5 consecutive days** are 28°C, 30°C, 32°C, 31°C, and 29°C.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a94a80a9b8cc7573de0d1901f130e5cd919d357868afeb92f30d04c0446744f.png] 

⇒ Sum of temperatures = 28 + 30 + 32 + 31 + 29

⇒ Sum = 150°C

⇒ Number of days = 5

⇒ Average = 150 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 30°C

**∴ The correct answer is 30°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Property

The algebraic sum of the **deviations** of a set of values from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Effect of Change in Origin

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from every observation, the **new average** will also be increased or decreased by 'k'.

Weighted Average

When observations have different levels of importance, the average is calculated as Σwx ÷ Σw, where 'w' is the **weight** assigned to each value 'x'.</p

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 1032 km in 8 hours. The speed of a train is double the speed of the car. One-third the speed of the train is equal to the speed of a bike. How much distance will the bike cover in 17 hours?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Speed of Car** = 1032 ÷ 8 = 129 kmph.

**Speed of Train** = 2 × 129 = 258 kmph.

**Speed of Bike** = 1/3 × 258 = 86 kmph.

**Distance by Bike** = 86 × 17 = 1462 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 1462 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Car Distance** = 1032 km, **Car Time** = 8 hours.

**Formula Used:**

**Speed** = Distance ÷ Time

**Distance** = Speed × Time
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e417bd8e46944b4ca89a222810deccaf0b277f7172392857799336b04a52b45b.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed of Car** = 1032 ÷ 8 = 129 kmph

⇒ **Speed of Train** = 2 × 129 = 258 kmph

⇒ **Speed of Bike** = 258 ÷ 3 = 86 kmph

⇒ **Distance covered by Bike in 17 hours** = 86 × 17

⇒ **Distance** = 1462 km

**∴ The correct answer is 1462 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert **kmph** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **kmph**, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds **x** and **y**, **Average Speed** = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

In the **same direction**, subtract speeds (u − v). In the **opposite direction**, add speeds (u + v).</p

questions.question: If at the same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is 40 and compound interest, compounded annually, is 42, then what is the principal (in)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Rate of Interest (R)** = [2 × (CI − SI) ÷ SI] × 100

⇒ R = [2 × (42 − 40) ÷ 40] × 100 = (4 ÷ 40) × 100 = 10%

**Principal (P)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (40 × 100) ÷ (10 × 2) = 4000 ÷ 20 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Simple Interest (SI) = 40, Compound Interest (CI) = 42, Time (T) = 2 years.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; CI − SI = Interest on first year SI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91e42381e13ad7449abc9401f5c095989b91467f02338d1b7369cb48761beccd.png] 

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) = 42 − 40 = 2

⇒ This difference 2 is the **interest** earned on the first year SI (20).

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (2 ÷ 20) × 100 = 10%

⇒ Since SI for 1 year is 20: 20 = (P × 10 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = P ÷ 10

⇒ P = 20 × 10 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference (D) is calculated as D = P(R/100)².

Relation for 2 years

The ratio of CI to SI for 2 years is CI/SI = (200 + R) / 200.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference is calculated as D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).</p

questions.question:
A hemispherical bowl has a 3.5 cm radius. It is to be painted inside as well as outside. Find the cost of painting it at the rate of ₹17 per 10 cm².

(Use pi = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total surface area to be painted (Inside + Outside) = 2 × 2πr² = 4πr².

Radius (r) = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm.

Total Area = 4 × (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2) = 154 cm².

Cost = (154 ÷ 10) × 17 = 15.4 × 17 = ₹261.8.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹261.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = **3.5 cm**

Rate of painting = **₹17 per 10 cm²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ddfc07e227d7d63f25784768a492f264f7f8e029742a129f8228aa4477b35528.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of hemisphere = 2πr²

Total painting area = Inside CSA + Outside CSA = 2πr² + 2πr² = **4πr²**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Area = 4 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5

⇒ Total Area = 4 × (22/7) × 12.25

⇒ Total Area = 154 cm²

⇒ Cost of painting 10 cm² = ₹17

⇒ Cost of painting 1 cm² = ₹1.7

⇒ Total Cost = 154 × 1.7

⇒ Total Cost = ₹261.8

**∴ The correct answer is ₹261.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of Sphere

Total surface area of a full sphere is 4πr².

Total Surface Area of Hemisphere

For a solid hemisphere, TSA = CSA + Area of base = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr².

Volume of Hemisphere

The volume of a hemisphere is (2/3)πr³.

questions.question: Find the value of (0.54)³ + (0.46)³
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **a = 0.54** and **b = 0.46**. Observe that **a + b = 0.54 + 0.46 = 1**.

Using the identity **a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)**, where the sum factor is **1**.

The value is simply **(0.54² − 0.54 × 0.46 + 0.46²) = 0.2916 − 0.2484 + 0.2116**.

This simplifies to **0.0432 + 0.2116 = 0.2548**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.2548.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression to evaluate is **(0.54)³ + (0.46)³**.

**Step 1:** Calculate the **cube** of the first term.

⇒ 0.54 × 0.54 = 0.2916

⇒ 0.2916 × 0.54 = **0.157464**

**Step 2:** Calculate the **cube** of the second term.

⇒ 0.46 × 0.46 = 0.2116

⇒ 0.2116 × 0.46 = **0.097336**

**Step 3:** Find the **sum** of the two results.

⇒ Value = 0.157464 + 0.097336

⇒ Value = **0.2548**

**∴ The correct answer is 0.2548.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Cubes

The formula is **a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)**. This is very useful when **a + b** results in a simple integer like 1 or 10.

Algebraic Identity for Difference of Cubes

The formula is **a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)**, which is the counterpart for subtraction of cubic terms.

BODMAS in Simplification

Always prioritize **Exponents (Powers/Orders)** before performing addition or subtraction in expressions like **xⁿ + yⁿ**.</p

questions.question: Hari travels from City A to City B. If Hari drives his car at 1/4 of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 39 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Hari would take to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Speed Ratio** (Normal : New) = 4 : 1

**Time Ratio** (Normal : New) = 1 : 4 (Since Time ∝ 1/Speed for constant distance)

Difference in time units = 4 − 1 = 3 units

Given difference = 39 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 39 ÷ 3 = 13 minutes

**Normal Time** (1 unit) = 13 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 13 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05d8249cbc308d3a6123d13da5341c19971779385cc493a5f675745aa5a00e3e.png] 
**Given:**

Normal speed = S, New speed = S/4

Time difference (Δt) = 39 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let normal time be T. Then new time = T + 39

⇒ Since Distance is constant, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

⇒ S × T = (S/4) × (T + 39)

⇒ 4T = T + 39

⇒ 3T = 39

⇒ T = 13 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 13 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the **distance** is constant, the time taken is inversely proportional to the speed (T ∝ 1/S). If speed becomes 1/n times, time becomes n times.

Late/Early Concept Formula

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| ] × Difference in time. This is useful for finding the actual distance between two points.</p

questions.question: If 22% of a number is equal to (4)/(9) th of another number, what is the ratio to the second number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the percentages and fractions directly: 22% × **First Number** = 4/9 × **Second Number**.

22/100 × A = 4/9 × B ⇒ 11/50 × A = 4/9 × B.

Ratio A : B = (4 × 50) : (11 × 9) = 200 : 99.

**∴ The correct answer is 200:99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 22% of **First Number** (x) = 4/9 of **Second Number** (y).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9a9f6764af16372ee59a66047d766ad8fe222b14c5103f02e4b681f0dd2a1b7.png] 

**Formula Used:** Ratio x : y = (Value attached to y) : (Value attached to x) when equating products.

⇒ 22% × x = (4/9) × y

⇒ (22/100) × x = (4/9) × y

⇒ (11/50) × x = (4/9) × y

⇒ x/y = (4/9) ÷ (11/50)

⇒ x/y = (4/9) × (50/11)

⇒ x/y = 200/99

**∴ The correct answer is 200:99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert x% to a fraction, divide by 100. Example: 22% = 22/100 = 11/50.

Ratio and Proportion Property

If Ax = By, then the ratio x : y is B : A. This is used to solve **equated quantities** efficiently.</p

questions.question: The average weight of 14 boys in a class is 40.25 kg and that of the remaining 4 boys is 38 kg. Find the average weight (in kg, rounded off to two decimal place) of all the boys in the class.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **number of boys** = 14 : 4 = 7 : 2.

Assume **base average** = 38 kg.

Deviation of 14 boys = 40.25 − 38 = +2.25 kg.

Total deviation = 14 × 2.25 = 31.5 kg.

Average increase = 31.5 ÷ 18 = 1.75 kg.

**Final Average** = 38 + 1.75 = 39.75 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average weight** of first 14 boys = 40.25 kg

**Average weight** of remaining 4 boys = 38 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9059688428a78b35b029fa31eec6144b23c0f90cdc4ad58ec6e363257877fd7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total weight** of 14 boys = 14 × 40.25 = 563.5 kg

⇒ **Total weight** of 4 boys = 4 × 38 = 152 kg

⇒ **Total number of boys** = 14 + 4 = 18 boys

⇒ **Total weight** of class = 563.5 + 152 = 715.5 kg

⇒ **Required Average weight** = 715.5 ÷ 18

⇒ Average weight = 39.75 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Properties of Average

If every observation is increased by a constant k, the **new average** also increases by k. The average always lies between the minimum and maximum values of the data set.

Deviation Concept

Net deviation about the average is always zero. This principle is used to solve **mixture and average** problems faster by assuming a middle value as the mean.</p

questions.question: Find the roots of the equation 5x² - 11x + 2 = 0 by factorisation method.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the equation 5x² − 11x + 2 = 0, find two numbers whose **product** is 10 (5 × 2) and **sum** is −11.

The required numbers are −10 and −1.

To find the roots directly, divide these factors by the coefficient of x² (which is 5) and **reverse the signs**.

Roots = −(−10 ÷ 5) = 2 and −(−1 ÷ 5) = 1/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5, 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** 5x² − 11x + 2 = 0

In the **factorisation method**, we split the middle term (−11x) into two terms such that their sum is −11x and their product is (5x²) × 2 = 10x².

⇒ 5x² − 10x − x + 2 = 0

⇒ 5x(x − 2) − 1(x − 2) = 0

⇒ (5x − 1)(x − 2) = 0

Now, set each factor to zero to find the roots:

⇒ 5x − 1 = 0

⇒ 5x = 1

⇒ x = 1/5

And,

⇒ x − 2 = 0

⇒ x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5, 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discriminant (D)

The term D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of roots. If D > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are real and equal; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.

Quadratic Formula

Roots can also be found using x = (−b ± √D) ÷ 2a.

Sum and Product of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.</p

questions.question: Five times the present age of Vashnavi is 18 years more than seven times the present age of Sooraj, and eight times the present age of Sooraj is 17 years less than five times the present age of Vashnavi. What is the sum of the present ages (in years) of Vashnavi and Sooraj?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **V** be Vashnavi age and **S** be Sooraj age.

From given: 5V − 7S = 18 and 5V − 8S = 17.

Subtracting the equations: (5V − 7S) − (5V − 8S) = 18 − 17 ⇒ S = 1.

Substitute S = 1 in 5V − 8S = 17 ⇒ 5V − 8 = 17 ⇒ 5V = 25 ⇒ V = 5.

Sum of ages = 5 + 1 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

5 × **Vashnavi age** = 7 × **Sooraj age** + 18

8 × **Sooraj age** = 5 × **Vashnavi age** − 17

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Vashnavi age be **V** and Sooraj age be **S**.

⇒ 5V = 7S + 18 --- (i)

⇒ 8S = 5V − 17 --- (ii)

⇒ Substitute 5V from (i) into (ii):

⇒ 8S = (7S + 18) − 17

⇒ 8S = 7S + 1

⇒ **S = 1 year**

⇒ Put S = 1 in (i): 5V = 7(1) + 18

⇒ 5V = 25 ⇒ **V = 5 years**

⇒ Sum = V + S = 5 + 1 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 2184, (2) 2800, (3) 1264, (4) 2349.

**Formula:** Divisibility by 12 ⇒ Divisibility by **co-prime factors** 3 and 4.

⇒ Checking **2184**: Last two digits are 84. 84 ÷ 4 = 21 (Divisible by 4).

⇒ Sum of digits of 2184 = 2 + 1 + 8 + 4 = 15. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ Checking **2800**: Sum = 2 + 8 + 0 + 0 = 10 (Not divisible by 3).

⇒ Checking **1264**: Sum = 1 + 2 + 6 + 4 = 13 (Not divisible by 3).

⇒ Checking **2349**: Last digit is odd (Not divisible by 4).

**∴ The correct answer is 2184.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the **last two digits** are divisible by 4 or are double zeros (00).

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number, check divisibility by its **co-prime** factors (e.g., 6 = 2 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5).</p

questions.question: The mean of data is 56, and its median is 76. The mode (using empirical relation) of the data is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**.

Substitute the given values: **Mode** = 3(76) − 2(56).

**Mode** = 228 − 112 = 116.

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 56

**Median** of the data = 76

**Formula Used:**

The **empirical relationship** between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is given by:

**Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cbd7ded878b5d051fcbd141909ba4b6bda7430fba6521d6057274b5b8933793.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × 76 − 2 × 56

⇒ **Mode** = 228 − 112

⇒ **Mode** = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

The formula **Mode** = 3 **Median** − 2 **Mean** is used for **moderately skewed** distributions.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a **perfectly symmetrical** distribution, the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (**Mean** = **Median** = **Mode**).

Skewness and Central Tendency

In a **positively skewed** distribution, **Mean** > **Median** > **Mode**. In a **negatively skewed** distribution, **Mode** > **Median** > **Mean**.</p

questions.question: If (x + 1/x) = 9 then (x² + 1/x²) is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the value of **x + 1/x = k**, then the value of **x² + 1/x² = k² − 2**.

In this question, **k = 9**.

∴ **x² + 1/x² = 9² − 2**

⇒ **81 − 2 = 79**

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The value of **x + 1/x = 9**.

**Formula Used:**

We use the **algebraic identity**: **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

**Calculations:**

Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ **(x + 1/x)² = 9²**

⇒ **x² + (1/x)² + 2 × x × (1/x) = 81**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² + 2 = 81**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 81 − 2**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 79**

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

If **x + 1/x = k**, then the value of **x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k**.

Subtraction Identity

If **x − 1/x = k**, then the value of **x² + 1/x² = k² + 2**.

Higher Power (Power of 4)

To find **x⁴ + 1/x⁴**, take the result of **x² + 1/x²** (say m), then calculate **m² − 2**.</p

questions.question: If A's salary is 51% more than that of B, then by what percentage is B's salary less than that of A (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **A** is **r%** more than **B**, then **B** is less than **A** by [r / (100 + r)] × 100%.

Required percentage = [51 / (100 + 51)] × 100

⇒ 5100 ÷ 151 ≈ 33.77%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.77%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bdc251cd891ee50f563c0d1a10e40ef57f3fb11a70368515d691f272019da7e4.png] 

**Given:**

Let **B's salary** = 100

**A's salary** is 51% more than **B**.

⇒ **A's salary** = 100 + 51% of 100 = 100 + 51 = 151

**Calculations:**

Difference between **A** and **B** = 151 − 100 = 51

Percentage by which **B** is less than **A** = (Difference / **A's salary**) × 100

⇒ Required % = (51 / 151) × 100

⇒ Required % = 5100 / 151

⇒ Required % = 33.7748...

Rounding to two decimal places, we get 33.77%.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.77%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change Comparison

When comparing two quantities, if A is x% more than B, then B is [x / (100 + x)] × 100% less than A.

Base Change Rule

Percentage is always calculated relative to the **base value**. When finding 'less than A', **A's value** becomes the denominator.

Inverse Case

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x / (100 − x)] × 100% more than A.</p

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 8 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 16 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be three-fourth filled, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **Filling rate** − **Emptying rate**.

Let **Total capacity** (LCM of 8 and 16) = 16 units.

Filling pipe efficiency = 16 ÷ 8 = 2; Emptying pipe efficiency = 16 ÷ 16 = 1.

Combined efficiency = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour.

Time for 3/4 filled = (3/4 × 16) ÷ 1 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 8 hours, Emptying time = 16 hours.

**Formula Used:** Work = Efficiency × Time; Net Efficiency = (1/Filling time) − (1/Emptying time).

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (hrs)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Filling Pipe 8 16 units +2 
 Emptying Pipe 16 −1 

⇒ **Combined efficiency** of both pipes = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Target volume to be filled = 3/4 × Total Capacity

⇒ Target volume = 3/4 × 16 = 12 units.

⇒ Time taken = Target volume ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

Filling pipes (inlets) have **positive efficiency**, while emptying pipes (outlets) have **negative efficiency**.

Net Work Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y). If x < y, the tank will eventually fill.

Fractional Filling

To find time for a specific fraction of the tank, multiply the total fill time by that **fractional value**.</p
